name: Details
summary: Use details to let users reveal optional supporting information without distracting from the main task.
whenToUse: Use for optional help or additional context that only some users need.
Use when the summary alone clearly explains what will be revealed.
whenNotToUse: Do not hide information most users need to understand or complete the task.
Do not hide validation errors, eligibility conditions or important consequences.
Do not use several details components when a clearer page structure would be easier to scan.

anatomy.name: Details element
anatomy.description: The native details element provides disclosure behaviour without GOV.UK JavaScript.

anatomy.name: Summary
anatomy.description: A native summary contains a short, descriptive govuk-details__summary-text label.

anatomy.name: Details text
anatomy.description: The revealed content sits in govuk-details__text.

variants.name: Closed by default
variants.use: Optional supporting content that is not required immediately.

variants.name: Open by default
variants.use: An exceptional case where the native open attribute is justified by the current context.

behaviour: Use the browser's native details and summary disclosure; no GOV.UK JavaScript module is required.
Do not replace summary with a generic div or custom click handler.
Content remains available in browsers that expose the native element without CSS.
accessibility: Keep the native elements and visible focus treatment.
Make the summary meaningful when read independently and avoid duplicate summaries on a page.
Ensure revealed interactive content follows the summary in a logical keyboard order.
content: Write the summary as a concise label for the hidden content, such as “Help with nationality”.
Keep the revealed answer focused and move essential instructions into the main page content.
